text: Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Luton Town and Liverpool at Kenilworth Road.
The hosts' return to top-flight football after a 31-year exodus has endured a tricky start, currently in the bottom three having won just one of their 10 games.
Much was made of Kenilworth Road and its hostile atmosphere towards away teams, yet the Hatters are yet to win there this season.
However, a victory here would take Luton out of the relegation zone and up to 17th.

Liverpool have started the campaign superbly, winning seven of their 10 games and taking 23 points from a possible 30 to leave them fourth in the Premier League, four points off leaders Manchester City heading into this game.
The Reds were trophyless last term for just the second time in five seasons, but their start to this one has fans optimistic of their chances of claiming silverware come the end of the campaign.

Rob Edwards makes just the one change from his team's last outing, a 3-1 defeat at Aston Villa, as Townsend comes in for Brown for his first Luton start having signed for the Hatters as a free agent in October.

Doughty has been a key player for Edwards' men this season, coming into the weekend with the second most chances created from set plays (14) behind James Ward-Prowse (16), while only Kieran Trippier (31) had completed more crosses than the Luton man (23).

Jurgen Klopp rung the changes for the 2-1 win over Bournemouth in the EFL Cup in midweek, and his big stars return for this one as the likes of Alisson, Salah and Van Dijk come back into the team, while Mac Allister, Gravenberch, Alexander-Arnold and Konate also start.
Nunez came off the bench to score a stunning winner against the Cherries, and he is rewarded with a start up top for the Reds.

Gomez will start at left-back with Andy Robertson still absent through injury, while Diaz returns on the bench despite his father being kidnapped back in Colombia, an ongoing situation that had seen him miss Liverpool's last two fixtures.
The two teams make their way onto the pitch in front of a vociferous Kenilworth Road crowd.
The visitors kick us off and we are underway at a drizzly Kenilworth Road!

Perhaps to be expected with the teams' respective positions in the Premier League table, Liverpool have looked the more confident side in these opening exchanges, dominating possession and prying for an opening.
The first attempt of the contest goes to Luton as Barkley fires goalwards from outside of the box, though Alisson gets down well to make a comfortable save.
Much like his goal against Bournemouth in the EFL Cup in midweek, Nunez cuts onto his right foot and tries to curl home from distance, though Kaminski is able to tip wide.
Van Dijk comes into this match with 49 Premier League away wins and could become just the 16th player to reach 50 victories in the competition on the road with Liverpool.
It has been a very lively opening at Kenilworth Road with both teams looking to get on the front foot.
Will Liverpool's superior quality tell?
This is the first meeting between Luton and Liverpool in any competition since January 2008, with the Reds winning an FA Cup third-round replay 5-0 at Anfield.
Steven Gerrard scored a hat-trick in that game.
OFF THE BAR! Alexander-Arnold picks up possession out wide and spots Nunez, who has made a superb run in behind the Luton defence.
The right-back arrows a delightful pass into the path of the Uruguay international, who brings it down before firing goalwards.
However, much to Luton's relief, the ball comes off the top of the woodwork and flies over.
Ogbene shows a great burst of pace to get down the left and float a cross over, and Konate can only nod the ball on to Kabore at the back post.
The wing-back lets fly, but his effort is poor and soars high into the stands.
Nunez continues to be heavily involved as he again cuts in and fires, though Kaminski is equal to the task as he beats away from danger.
That is already Nunez's fourth shot of the game.
Nunez has now hit the woodwork twice as many times as any other player in the Premier League this season (four).
Twenty minutes on the clock at Kenilworth Road, and both teams have certainly had their chances.
Nunez went the closest when he struck the woodwork, though the scoreline remains 0-0.
Szoboszlai's free-kick delivery is headed out by Mengi, but only to the waiting Salah.
The winger hits it first time, but his effort is very poor and flies high over the crossbar.
Liverpool have lost just one of their last 10 meetings with the Hatters in all competitions (five wins, four draws), going down 3-1 at Kenilworth Road in February 1991.
Nunez shows a great leap to rise above Kabore and nod Salah's cross goalwards, but he cannot get his header on target and Kaminski watches it go over his crossbar.
Nunez has already had five shots, at least four more than any other player on the pitch.
His xG (expected goals) of 0.29 is almost double Luton's (0.15).
Luton are yet to keep a Premier League clean sheet in 10 games this season, the first time they have failed to manage a shutout in their opening 10 league games since 2019-20 in the Championship.
They have held firm so far here, though.
Edwards will be pleased with his team's display to this point, though he will be keen for more of an attacking threat having watched his side manage just one shot on target.
BIG SAVE! A brilliant injection of pace from Gravenberch sees him reach the edge of the Luton box, drawing out the defenders and creating the space to feed Jota.
The Portugal international pulls the trigger first time, firing towards the bottom corner, though Kaminski gets down to his right and paws it away.
The game is paused because Kabore seems to have something in his eye.
The right-back goes off to receive more treatment and Luton will have to defend a corner a man down.
The corner is floated over to the waiting Alexander-Arnold, but his powerful first-time volley is blocked by a crowded penalty area.
Kabore eventually comes back onto the field.
Luton have failed to score in any of their previous first halves at home in the Premier League, and are seven minutes away from doing so again.
Ogbene is fortunate not to receive a booking as a seemingly intentional handball halts a Liverpool counter-attack.
The visiting players are incensed.
A cross from the left is deflected to just outside the Liverpool box, where Barkley is waiting to let fly.
However, his effort is poor and the ball soars over Alisson's crossbar.
Nakamba receives the first booking of the game for a very heavy challenge on Mac Allister in midfield.
Liverpool want a red, but there is nothing doing despite a VAR check.
There will be two minutes of additional time at the end of this first half.
Ogbene's pace has been causing big problems for Liverpool, offering a real outlet for the Hatters as they look to relieve some of the pressure they have been under.
HALF-TIME: LUTON TOWN 0-0 LIVERPOOL
The half-time whistle blows as Luton and Liverpool head back to the changing rooms with the scoreline goalless.
Both have had chances, with Nunez going the closest when he struck the bar after Alexander-Arnold's excellent pass picked him out, while Barkley saw a shot saved by Alisson at the other end.
Kaminski made a couple of great stops, including a sublime save to deny Jota and ensure the Hatters got into the break at 0-0.
Luton have more than held their own, and Edwards will be pleased with how his side have played so far.
They have created just 0.17 xG, though, compared to 1.05 for Liverpool, so he will be keen for his team to conjure up more of an attacking threat after the interval.
The hosts get the ball rolling again for the second half.
Luton have now failed to score a first-half goal in 10 of their 11 games, more often than any other team in the Premier League this season.
Liverpool have started this second half brightly, looking to pin back their hosts and find a way through.
Nunez registered six shots in the first half, already more than he has managed in any single match in the Premier League this season.
Can the Uruguay international turn a plethora of efforts into the opening goal?
Ogbene cuts in and tries to curl into the far corner, but his effort is very tame and easily saved by Allison, who is yet to really be tested.
Mac Allister goes in the book for cynically wiping out Townsend as the former Everton man looked to launch a counter.
That yellow card means he is suspended for the home game with Brentford next weekend.
Kabore whips a dangerous delivery into the Liverpool penalty area, but Alisson is alert to come out of his goal and collect before any lurking Luton attacker can fire home.
Klopp will be wanting a couple of goals soon to stave off any late nerves, with Luton having scored six of their nine Premier League goals this season in the final 10 minutes of games.
Only Arsenal had scored more during that timeframe (seven) heading into the weekend's action.
Kabore stays down for a prolonged period after a thunderous collision with Gomez, who also went tumbling into the advertising boards on the left-hand side.
Both appear fine to continue, though.
Chong comes on for Townsend, who has acquitted himself well in his first start in 18 months.
Liverpool had 69.9 per cent possession over the opening 15 minutes of the second half, though Luton remain level.
The longer the score remains 0-0, the more confidence the hosts will have that they can potentially kick on and force a winner.
CHANCE! Ogbene again causes problems for the Liverpool defence as he makes it into the visitors' box.
He tries to cross, and though it is blocked, it falls into the path of Morris.
However, Alisson does brilliantly to race out and close the angle, eventually making an important stop to divert behind for a corner.
Szoboszlai is replaced by Elliott.
The Hungary international had not been his usual creative force in this game.
Jota makes way for Gakpo.
Gomez's shift at left-back is over, and he trudges off for Tsimikas.
BIG OPPORTUNITY! Elliott gets down the left before cutting back and floating a cross into the box.
It ends up falling to Gakpo, but the ball is just behind the Netherlands international and his acrobatic shot flies wide of the target.
He just could not quite get his feet sorted in time.
Alexander-Arnold loops a cross towards the back post for Salah, whose goalwards header is so poor that it ends up falling for Nunez.
It seems he cannot miss, but somehow the Uruguay international fires well over the crossbar.
It is an incredible miss, but fortunately the flag goes up for offside to somewhat spare his blushes.
HUGE STOP! Salah's perfectly weighted throughball finds Nunez in the Luton box, and he tries to catch out the goalkeeper by shooting early.
However, Kaminski is equal to the task and tips over.
It is all Liverpool at the moment!

Liverpool want a penalty as Van Dijk is hauled to the turf by Mengi with a corner coming over from the left, but the referee decides against awarding a spot-kick before a subsequent VAR check confirms his decision.
Nunez has now had an extraordinary nine attempts, hitting the target with three of them.
He has been a very busy man.
Morris has put in a decent shift for Luton up front, but now makes way for Adebayo.
Nunez's nine shots are the joint-most of any player in a Premier League match this season (Marcus Rashford v Brighton and Erling Haaland v West Ham – also nine).
KAMINSKI TO THE RESCUE! Gravenberch cuts onto his left foot and tries to catch out the Luton goalkeeper at his near post, but Kaminski is again alert to leap to his left and parry away from danger.
Ogebene has been Luton's most lively player, but he is replaced by Brown with just over 10 minutes to play.
GOAL!!! CHONG PUTS LUTON AHEAD!!! It comes from a Liverpool corner, which seems to deflect onto Barkley's arm.
While the visitors appeal for a penalty, Edwards' men charge forward on the counter and Barkley lays it to his right for Kabore.
The right-back keeps his composure to curl a cross into the path of Chong, and the substitute beats Alisson to the ball to poke home and spark wild celebrations from the home fans.
There is a VAR check, and though Dijk's header does seem to come off Barkley's arm, the VAR decides to award the goal and Luton are 1-0 up thanks to Chong's first Premier League goal!
Kabore did superbly to play a perfectly weighted cross into the path of Chong to fire past Alisson and into the back of the net.
Luton have scored seven goals in the last 15 minutes of the second half, only Arsenal (eight) have scored more in the Premier League this season.
Will another late salvo power the Hatters to victory?
Diaz makes his return off the bench, on in place of Gravenberch.
WIDE! Konate nips in front of Barkley to meet Tsimikas' cross from the left, and his header looks destined for the bottom corner with Kaminski at full stretch.
However, the ball flies just past the right post.
Luton have dropped very deep, daring Liverpool to try and break them down.
It is a risky tactic considering the quality Klopp boasts in his team.
Kabore is down after a coming-together with Tsimikas near the corner flag, clutching at his hamstring.
He has been brilliant in this game, including his excellent assist for what could be the winner.
Kabore is okay to continue, and the game resumes as we move into eight minutes of additional time at the end of this match.
Can Liverpool rescue a result?
Luton currently have the ball high up the pitch, exactly where they need it.
The home fans are willing them on to a result, one that is within touching distance.
GOAL!!! DIAZ EQUALISES FOR LIVERPOOL!!! INCREDIBLE!!! With all that is going on in his personal life, Diaz comes up big for his team at the crucial moment.

Elliott floats a superb cross over to the back post for Diaz, who leaps high above Kabore to reach the ball before nodding over Kaminski and in to make it 1-1! The winger celebrates by lifting up his shirt and showing a message for his missing father.
Elliott has been very lively since coming on, and it was his cross that unlocked the defence and allowed Diaz to head home.
Liverpool urgently want a winner in the closing minutes, while Luton are hanging on.
It is the visiting fans who are audible now, and they are urging their team on to try and find another goal.
Kabore receives the ball on the right-hand side of the box before firing at goal, but the angle is very tight and Alisson makes a comfortable save.
FULL-TIME: LUTON TOWN 1-1 LIVERPOOL
The full-time whistle blows as Luton and Liverpool share the spoils with a 1-1 draw at Kenilworth Road.

It could have been so much more for Luton, who had to soak up a lot of Liverpool pressure before a swift counter-attack gave them the lead with 10 minutes to play, Kabore flying forwards before curling a delightful cross into the middle for Chong to finish.
With an initial eight minutes added on, Luton looked like they were going to hold on.

However, in the fifth minute of that added time, Elliott arrowed a delivery to the back post, where Diaz leapt above Kabore before nodding past Kaminski and in, celebrating by lifting up his shirt to reveal a message in support of his missing father back home in Colombia.

The full-time whistle was greeted with cheers by the Luton fans, perhaps indicative of the momentum Liverpool were gaining as they looked for a winner, and the Hatters just about held on to secure a point, one that takes them out of the relegation zone and up to 17th.
Liverpool move up to third, above Arsenal on goals scored, and they turn their attentions to Europa League action next, travelling to take on Toulouse on Thursday.
For Luton, they will look to build on this result when they face Manchester United at Old Trafford next Saturday.
That is all we have from Kenilworth Road, so thanks for your company and goodbye!
